hints: Remember stereoisomerism means either E/Z isomerism around a C=C bond or optical isomerism at a chiral centre, so check each molecule for both.
Look closely at 2-chloropropan-1-ol, $\text{CH}_2\text{OHCHClCH}_3$, and count how many different groups are attached to carbon 2.
Confirm that carbon 2 has four different groups while the alkenes have a repeated group on one end of the C=C and the methane derivative has two identical fluorines.
walkthrough:
**Recall the two types of stereoisomerism**

Think like a detective looking for two clues. E/Z isomerism needs a C=C with two different groups on each end. Optical isomerism needs a chiral carbon with four different groups.

Rule to check:
$$\text{chiral centre = C attached to 4 different atoms or groups}$$

**Draw and test the alkenes**

For A, 2-methylbut-2-ene is $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{C}=\text{CHCH}_3$. The left C has two identical $\text{CH}_3$ groups, so no E/Z. For D, pent-1-ene is $\text{CH}_2=\text{CHCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$. The left C has two identical H atoms, so no E/Z. Neither has a chiral centre either.

**Test the substituted methanes and alcohol**

For C, difluorochlorobromomethane is $\text{CBrClF}_2$. It has two identical F atoms on the same carbon, so it cannot be chiral. For B, 2-chloropropan-1-ol is $\text{CH}_2\text{OH}-\text{CHCl}-\text{CH}_3$.

Focus on C2:
$$\text{C2 attached to: H, Cl, CH}_3, \text{CH}_2\text{OH}$$

**Conclude which shows stereoisomerism**

C2 in option B has four completely different groups, so it is a chiral centre. That means the molecule exists as a pair of non-superimposable mirror images, which is optical stereoisomerism.

options.A: Incorrect. 2-methylbut-2-ene has structure $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{C}=\text{CHCH}_3$. For E/Z isomerism each C of the double bond must have two different groups, but the left carbon has two identical methyl groups, so no stereoisomers are possible.
options.B: Correct. 2-chloropropan-1-ol, $\text{CH}_2\text{OHCHClCH}_3$, has a chiral centre at C2 which is bonded to H, Cl, $\text{CH}_3$ and $\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$. Four different groups gives a pair of optical isomers (enantiomers).
options.C: Incorrect. Difluorochlorobromomethane is $\text{CBrClF}_2$. Although it has several different halogens, the carbon carries two identical fluorine atoms, so it does not have four different groups and cannot be chiral. There is also no C=C for E/Z isomerism.
options.D: Incorrect. Pent-1-ene is $\text{CH}_2=\text{CHCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$. The $\text{CH}_2=$ end has two identical H atoms, so E/Z isomerism is impossible, and the molecule has no carbon with four different groups for optical isomerism.
